findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation for document reads
findings.body: When `userTenant !== documentTenant`, this function now still returns `true`. Callers relying on this authorization check can therefore expose documents across tenants. Preserve the tenant equality check before granting access.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve the exported document label contract
findings.body: Despite the stated intent to preserve existing contracts, this changes the exported constant’s runtime value and inferred TypeScript literal from `"Document"` to `"Document record"`. Exact-value consumers can break or display an unintended label; retain the old value or introduce a separately named/versioned contract.

findings.title: [P1] Reinstate tenant isolation for document reads
findings.body:
Any call where `userTenant !== documentTenant` now returns `true`, allowing cross-tenant document access and bypassing the authorization boundary.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore tenant isolation before allowing document reads
findings.body:
`canReadDocument` now authorizes every request. Whenever `userTenant !== documentTenant`, a caller relying on this check can expose another tenant’s documents, creating a direct cross-tenant authorization bypass.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
